proposals.before: In his seventeenth year of service he was posted as intendant of the Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou circuit in Guangdong.
proposals.after: In the seventeenth year he was posted as intendant of the Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou circuit in Guangdong.
proposals.reason: 十七年 continues the Jiaqing reign count from s0005, not years of personal service.

proposals.before: along the coast, Miao and Yao communities had become havens for fugitives, and he registered them all under the baojia system.
proposals.after: along the coast, civilian shed communities had become havens for fugitives, and he registered them all under the baojia system.
proposals.reason: 民寮 means civilian sheds/hut settlements, not Miao and Yao peoples.

proposals.before: coastal Miao and Yao inhabitants lived in places that became refuges for fugitives; he had them all registered in baojia.
proposals.after: coastal civilian shed inhabitants lived in places that became refuges for fugitives; he had them all registered in baojia.
proposals.reason: 民寮 means civilian sheds/hut settlements, not Miao and Yao peoples.

proposals.before: In the eighteenth year he was posted as grain intendant of Hunan; after mourning his adoptive mother he served successively as intendant of the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiazhou circuit in Guangdong, intendant of the Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji circuit in Shandong, provincial judge of Hubei, and provincial treasurer of Gansu.
proposals.after: In the eighteenth year he was posted as grain intendant of Hunan; after mourning his birth parents he served successively as intendant of the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jiazhou circuit in Guangdong, intendant of the Yan-Yi-Cao-Ji circuit in Shandong, provincial judge of Hubei, and provincial treasurer of Gansu.
proposals.reason: 本生父母 means birth parents, not an adoptive mother.

proposals.before: At that time Yao in Guiyang, Changde, and other districts rose in support of the rebels; the Changde naval forces and the Jingzhou garrison troops were unskilled in mountain warfare—when Kun arrived he dismissed them all, transferred troops from the Zhenxiong Miao frontier, garrisoned the strategic passes, practiced scorched-earth defense, and held the rebels at bay.
proposals.after: At that time Yao in Guiyang, Changde, and other districts rose in support of the rebels; the Changde naval forces and the Jingzhou garrison troops were unskilled in mountain warfare—when Kun arrived he dismissed them all, transferred troops from the Zhen'gan Miao frontier, garrisoned the strategic passes, practiced scorched-earth defense, and held the rebels at bay.
proposals.reason: 鎮筸 is Zhen'gan on the Hunan Miao frontier, not Zhenxiong.

proposals.before: At that time Yao in Guiyang, Changde, and elsewhere rose in response to the rebels; Changde naval forces and garrison troops from Jingzhou were unused to mountain warfare—when Kun arrived he dismissed them all, transferred Zhenxiong Miao frontier troops, garrisoned strategic passes, practiced fortified defense and scorched earth, and held the enemy at bay.
proposals.after: At that time Yao in Guiyang, Changde, and elsewhere rose in response to the rebels; Changde naval forces and garrison troops from Jingzhou were unused to mountain warfare—when Kun arrived he dismissed them all, transferred Zhen'gan Miao frontier troops, garrisoned strategic passes, practiced fortified defense and scorched earth, and held the enemy at bay.
proposals.reason: 鎮筸 is Zhen'gan on the Hunan Miao frontier, not Zhenxiong.

proposals.before: He petitioned to reduce salt prices and on his own authority halted unauthorized tax increases.
proposals.after: He petitioned to reduce salt prices; smuggling ceased and tax revenue increased.
proposals.reason: 私絕課增 means private/smuggled salt stopped and tax receipts rose, not that he halted tax increases on his own authority.

proposals.before: Zuo Zongtang and Hu Linyi both knew him before he had risen to prominence, and marriage ties were formed between their families; both later became famous statesmen.
proposals.after: Zuo Zongtang and Hu Linyi were both known to him before they had risen to prominence, and marriage ties were formed between their families; both later became famous statesmen.
proposals.reason: 識之未遇 means Tao recognized them before THEY had risen, not that they knew him before he rose.

proposals.before: Zuo Zongtang and Hu Linyi both knew him before he had risen to prominence and formed marriage ties; later both became famous ministers.
proposals.after: Zuo Zongtang and Hu Linyi were both known to him before they had risen to prominence and marriage ties were formed; later both became famous ministers.
proposals.reason: 識之未遇 means Tao recognized them before they had risen.

decisions.reason: s0002 lists 曾勝; standard Mandarin romanization is Zeng Sheng, so idiomatic Ceng Sheng is a transcription error and the proposed replacement is accurate.
The same 曾勝 in s0002 requires Zeng, not Ceng, in the literal field; the proposed spelling corrects the mistranscription without other change.
s0011 opens with 十七年 as a reign-year date continuing the Jiaqing chronology, not years of personal service; dropping 'of service' restores the correct dating sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十七年，出為廣東惠潮嘉道

decisions.reason: s0013 has 沿海民寮居; 民寮 are civilian shed/hut settlements, not Miao and Yao peoples, so the proposed wording removes an invented ethnic reading.
Literal likewise misreads 民寮 as Miao and Yao; replacing with civilian shed inhabitants matches the Chinese without adding new error.
s0064 has 丁本生父母憂; 本生父母 are birth parents, not an adoptive mother, and the proposed plural 'birth parents' is accurate and grammatical.
s0103 transfers 鎮筸苗疆兵; 鎮筸 is the Hunan Miao-frontier Zhen'gan garrison, not Yunnan Zhenxiong, so the place-name repair is correct.
The literal field has the same 鎮筸 misread as Zhenxiong; Zhen'gan is the supported reading of the Chinese place name.
s0141 私絕課增 is a result clause: smuggling ceased and the salt tax quota/revenue rose, not that Tao on his own authority halted tax increases; the proposal restores that sense.
In Tao Shu's biography, 皆識之未遇 means he recognized Zuo and Hu before they had risen (未遇 paired with 後俱為名臣), not that they knew him before he rose; the proposed wording corrects agent and patient.
Literal repeats the same reversed recognition; making Zuo and Hu the ones not yet risen matches 識之未遇 and 後俱為名臣.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皆識之未遇，結為婚姻，後俱為名臣

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows alternate Ceng Sheng arose only from mistranscribing 曾勝; s0002 supports Zeng Sheng (c0017), not a separate Ceng alias.
Accepted r0006 shows 'adoptive mother' was created solely by the bad translation of 本生父母; the source supports biological mother (c0074), not an adoptive-mother name claim.
